items.title: Jimmy Owens interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: Randy Weston was one of my mentors also. He taught me a lot about the business — publishing, and how publishing works.

ctx.x: That’s great. Did the musicians that you met, either as teachers or just in the clubs, did you get a sense of them instilling you with other things, just besides the playing of the music? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well I can’t say — I mentioned that Donald Byrd was my mentor. And he instilled in me what being a professional musician was. He taught me about the business. He was the first to start that, let’s put it that way. And made me aware about copyright, and about taking care of business. And then there were other musicians who were equally as important and took it another step. Randy Weston was one of my mentors also. items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had learned this stuff from Donald Byrd and Randy Weston... Randy Weston gave me a stack of about an inch of his lead sheets... he would tell me things about publishing... I recall how Randy Weston and Donald Byrd... gave me information freely.

ctx.x: I had written arrangements for other small groups that we had. You know, me and Joe Orange had a group that had trumpet, trombone, alto saxophone, tenor saxophone, and I was writing arrangements for that type of thing. But, this was the first time I had written a big band arrangement, and it did sound very, very good- you know, as I can remember. Hamp loved it. Where we came into New York we worked at the Metropole bar. We would do four sets a night and he would play “Complicity,” by that time I had two…

play that song.” They’d say, “Well, we don’t have any lead sheets.” When this situation came up with Lionel Hampton, I just remembered all the stuff that I had learned. I said, “You go record it. I was going to give you the publishing, but you’re saying that Hampton’s name is going to be on it? No!” So I took my arrangements back, and from that day on I had about three months more that I stayed with the band. We did a trip out to Las Vegas and California.
